q: A soil and climate survey in the late 1970s singled out a gravel terrace at the southern end of the North Island as the country's most promising Pinot Noir ground, and vines went in within two years. Which district?
exp: The survey weighed rainfall, temperature and soils against Burgundy and pointed at this one terrace, which makes it a rare case of a wine region founded on a report rather than on habit. A handful of small wineries were established there around 1980 and the reputation followed inside a decade.

q: How does Botrytis cinerea concentrate the juice inside a berry?
opts: It converts the grape's acid into sugar
It thickens the skin and traps water inside
It ferments part of the sugar while still on the vine
It pierces the skin so water evaporates away
exp: The fungus perforates the skin with its filaments and the berry shrivels, concentrating sugar, acid and flavour together. It also contributes honey, ginger and dried apricot of its own.

q: A guest asks for the Japanese spirit distilled from barley, sweet potato or rice. What should you point them toward?
exp: Shochu goes through a still and typically arrives at around 25 percent, so it is not sake at all. Mirin is a sweet cooking wine and amazake is barely alcoholic.

q: Freshly pressed white juice is left overnight in a chilled tank and the bright fraction is drawn off a sludge of pulp and skin fragments in the morning. What is that step called?
exp: Fermenting very dirty juice gives a coarse wine that can turn bitter and sulphurous, so the heavy solids are dropped out first. A little cloudiness is left on purpose, because juice cleaned absolutely spotless lacks the nutrients the yeast need and can struggle to finish.

q: Hot, low country in the Tulum Valley supplies Syrah along with much of the base wine for Argentine vermouth and brandy. Which province is it?
exp: San Juan lies immediately north of Mendoza and is both hotter and lower. Its more serious Syrah comes from the higher Pedernal and Calingasta valleys rather than the Tulum floor.

q: Set the French, Italian, Spanish and Portuguese systems side by side and the vocabulary differs completely while the structure matches almost step for step. What accounts for that?
opts: All four were drafted together by a single commission in Brussels
The other three were built on the French model and share one framework
The resemblance is coincidental, since each was built in isolation
All four were modelled on a ripeness ladder
exp: France wrote the modern pattern first, a delimited place bound to a production rulebook, and its neighbours adopted it over the following decades, long before any European harmonisation existed. The later European layer then tidied the categories without disturbing the shape underneath, which is why a student who learns one of the four can read the others quickly.

q: Clay-rich soils weathered from a rock quite unlike the Swartland's shale give the Hemel-en-Aarde its ability to hold water through a dry summer. Which rock?
exp: Bokkeveld shale weathers to heavy clay, and clay is what lets an unirrigated vine on a warm slope reach harvest in balance. It is much younger than the Malmesbury shale of the Swartland and behaves very differently in the vineyard.

q: Victor Hugo put the wine of one Rhone village into Les Miserables, and Saint-Joseph later grew out of its slopes. Which village?
exp: The wine of Mauves was famous long before the appellation was created in 1956. The granite core of Saint-Joseph still lies around that village and its neighbour Tournon.

q: A single obscure white grape survives in one small appellation near Blois and almost nowhere else on earth. Which variety?
exp: Cour-Cheverny exists solely to protect it. The wine is lean, waxy and slow to open, and neighbouring Cheverny uses Sauvignon Blanc instead.

q: Which white grape stands behind the wines of Gavi?
exp: Gavi lies in the southeast of Piedmont near the Ligurian border. Cortese gives a dry, lean, citrus-driven wine that traditionally went to the seafood restaurants of the coast.

q: One first course on tonight's menu will strip the fruit out of a bone-dry white and leave it tasting sharp and hollow. Which is it?
exp: Very ripe melon is sweet enough to out-sweeten a dry wine, and the ham beside it does not change that. The other three are salty, savoury or saline, and every one of those flatters a dry white rather than fighting it.

q: Four items appear on a bottle of European wine: the name of the bottler, the alcoholic strength, the volume and the harvest year. Which one of them is the producer free to leave off?
exp: A year is an optional particular, which is why a wine may quite legally be sold carrying none at all. The other three are obligatory on every bottle, and a wine that omits any of them cannot be put on shelf.
